decisions.name: ContentAddressedIdentityIsBytesNotLabels
decisions.what: A file's identity is (crc32, size_bytes); the CRC32 is also embedded in folder/file names (~XXXXXXXX) and re-derived from the on-disk bytes at every stage. Names are derived data, never the source of truth.
why: The whole point of the project: the same title ripped twice is two distinct rows, a renamed or relocated folder is still the same row. Identity survives every rename because it is a hash of the video bytes, not a path.
files has UNIQUE (crc32, size_bytes); ON CONFLICT upserts. That pair is the primary identity everywhere downstream (associations.file_id, probe_cache, move verification).

Folder-embedded CRC (parseFolderName reading ~XXXXXXXX) is a CONVENIENCE for fast skip and human inspection, NOT trusted: processOne re-probes and corrects a folder whose claimed CRC disagrees with the bytes.
Consequence: every CRC comparison in the pipeline is uppercase (runRhashCrc32 uppercases+trims); any code that introduces a lowercase or untrimmed CRC will silently fail to match.

decisions.name: StageAndMediaKindPartitionOneFilesTable
decisions.what: One files table is partitioned by two columns: stage (staging -> buffer -> library) and media_kind (movie | episode). The resolvers select on these, they are not separate tables.
why: Movies and TV share the same files table, the same identity model, and the same three-directory discipline; only the two partition columns separate them.
resolve matches media_kind='movie' AND stage<>'buffer' (selectUnresolvedSql); tv-resolve matches media_kind='episode' AND stage='staging' (selectUnresolvedTvSql).

stage='buffer' is deliberately EXCLUDED from movie resolve: once rename has written a folder into the buffer, its identity comes from the NFO rename wrote, not from a fresh TMDB match. Re-resolving a buffered file would fight the rename that already happened.
rename selects stage='staging' (selectRenamableSql / selectEpisodeRenamableSql), move flips rows to stage='library'. The lifecycle is encoded in this column, not in code flow.

decisions.name: MoveBlastRadiusIsOneFolderUnderRoot
decisions.what: move/tv-move only ever WRITE under the configured library root and only ever DELETE from the buffer; every destination is guarded by enforceUnderRoot before any filesystem mutation.
why: This is the single most dangerous verb in the system: it relocates real media and deletes the source. The safety property is mechanical, not careful coding: enforceUnderRoot rejects any destination not prefixed by libraryRoot + '/'.

move additionally aborts if the destination folder already exists, so it can never overwrite an existing library folder. The blast radius of one movie move is exactly: one folder added to library, one removed from buffer.
tv-move is a deliberately WIDER blast radius (it merges into an existing show folder via mergeTree), but still never overwrites an existing episode file and still only writes under tvLibrary.

The library root comes from UNIDORK_PATH_LIBRARY / UNIDORK_PATH_TV_LIBRARY (set from nix/config.nix). Those env vars are the ONLY thing controlling where move writes; this is why the README tells you to echo them before the first production move.

decisions.name: IdentityVerifiedBySizeNotByRehash
decisions.what: At promotion, a file's stored CRC is trusted as long as the on-disk size equals the stored size_bytes. There is no re-hash at move time; on size mismatch (or missing row) the update falls back to a name-based path update.
why: Re-running rhash on every file at promotion would double the I/O cost of the slowest part of the pipeline for files that have not changed since probe. Size equality is a cheap proxy: a file whose byte count is unchanged has overwhelmingly not had its CRC change.

verifyFile / verifyEpisode return (path, diskOk, identOpt) where diskOk is purely the size comparison. updateMovieFile / updateEpisode then branch: verified -> update files row by (crc, size); unverified -> update by old path string, and print a WARN.

The honest hole: a file corrupted or swapped in place at exactly the same byte length would pass verification with a stale CRC. This is accepted as vanishingly unlikely against the I/O savings. See open issue NoRematchGateAtPromotion for the related trust of the NFO id.

decisions.name: AtomicRenameOrRsyncPartialThenCommit
decisions.what: Same-filesystem transfers use an atomic mv -T; cross-filesystem transfers rsync into a .unidork-partial staging dir under the library root, then mv-commit into place, then delete the source. Crashed partials are swept on the next run.
why: A cross-device move is not atomic: a crash mid-copy would leave a half-written folder in the live library. Staging the copy under .unidork-partial and only mv-committing the completed copy makes the visible-in-library step atomic even across filesystems.

sameDevice compares stat %d (device numbers); a stat FAILURE returns false, which routes to the SAFER rsync-partial path rather than risking an atomic rename that would actually be a cross-device copy.

sweepPartial removes the whole .unidork-partial tree at the start of a non-dry-run move, on the theory that any partial present is the debris of a previous crash, never a concurrent transfer (the pipeline is single-writer).
On a cross-device abort the SOURCE is left intact (delete only happens after a successful commit), so a failed move never loses data.

decisions.name: RuntimeNormalizedClusteringForEditions
decisions.what: Versions clusters a tmdb_id's copies into editions by normalizing each copy's runtime to a reference frame rate (24000/1001) and grouping copies whose normalized seconds are within 1.5% of each other.
why: The naive approach (group by raw duration) would split a PAL 25fps transfer and a 23.976fps transfer of the SAME cut into two editions because PAL speedup shortens the runtime by ~4%. normalizedSeconds multiplies durationSec by fps/referenceFps to cancel the speedup.

relativeClose uses a RELATIVE tolerance (d/hi <= sameCutTolerance = 1.5e-2), not an absolute second count, so the tolerance scales with film length: a 3-hour film tolerates more absolute drift than a 90-minute one.

The 1.5% threshold is tuned to merge frame-rate and minor-trim differences while still separating a genuine Director's/Extended cut (which differ by minutes, well outside 1.5%). See open issue DuplicatesNotRankedForUser for what clustering does NOT yet do.

decisions.name: DatabaseAndMetadataAreAbilitiesInterpretedAtRunBoundary
decisions.what: Per-file logic (resolveOne, runStep, etc.) is written against abilities (MovieCatalog/ResolveCatalog/MetaApi/TvCatalog/TvMetaApi/RenameCatalog/TvMoveCatalog). The real Postgres/HTTP handlers are installed only at the runWith / run boundary; the per-file functions never touch a connection directly.
why: This is what makes resolveOne and friends unit-testable with scripted pure handlers. The Resolve.resolveOne.* and Tv.Resolve.resolveOne.* tests install handlers that return canned TMDB responses and RECORD whether recordMatch was called, with zero database or network.

The effect rows in the signature (e.g. {MetaApi, ResolveCatalog}) are the contract: any handler satisfying them can drive the logic. The production handler (metaGo/catalogGo inside runWith) wires the ability to prepared statements; the test handler wires it to a tuple accumulator.

Consequence: reading a resolveOne body tells you the decision logic but NOT what hits the DB. The actual writes live in the handler arms of runWith, and the dry-run gate (see DryRunGatesWritesNotMetadata) lives in resolveOne but is enforced by simply not calling the ability.

decisions.name: DryRunGatesFilesystemAndAssociationsNotProbeOrCache
decisions.what: --dry-run suppresses filesystem operations and association/match writes, but probe rows, TMDB caches, and subtitle-search caches are STILL written during a dry run.
why: A dry run is meant to preview file movement and matching decisions safely, not to be a pure read. Probing and caching are idempotent, side-effect-free-on-the-library work whose results are valuable to keep even from a preview run.

resolveOne / Tv.Resolve.resolveOne gate recordMatch/recordEpisodeMatch on dryRun (the 'if dryRun then () else record...' pattern), but the surrounding runWith still fetches and caches TMDB details/search/season payloads regardless.
move/rename gate the actual mv/rsync/removeFile and the files-row promotion on dryRun, emitting WouldRename/WouldRemoveDuplicate outcomes instead.
Consequence: a dry run is NOT free of DB writes. It will populate probe_cache, tmdb_search_cache, tmdb_details_cache, etc. This is intentional but surprising; do not treat --dry-run as read-only.

openIssues.name: RelangDecisionComputedButNeverApplied
openIssues.what: Relang.decide produces a default-audio-track decision (SwitchTo / AlreadyCorrect / OriginalNotPresent / ...), but nothing in the pipeline remuxes or re-flags the file to apply it.
why: decide -> selectTrack -> bestOf is a complete, tested analysis: it picks the original-language, non-commentary, highest-channel/best-codec track and reports whether the current default is wrong. The result is a Decision value that is computed and then dropped.
There is no ffmpeg remux step and no mkvpropedit call anywhere that consumes a SwitchTo. The README lists this under 'What's next' as the first item.

Wiring it requires deciding WHEN to apply (at rename into buffer? at promotion?) and a mux/flag step that mutates the container, which crosses the line from metadata-only into byte-mutating territory and needs its own safety story.
blocking: actually correcting default audio tracks for foreign-language media

openIssues.name: NoSubtitleMuxingAndNoTvSubtitleFetchAtAll
openIssues.what: Movie subtitles are fetched from subdl and written as language-tagged SIDECAR files only; they are never muxed into the MKV, and the TV pipeline fetches no subtitles whatsoever.
why: fetchAndSaveByImdb/saveOneLanguage download and write '<base>.<lang>.<ext>' next to the video. maybeFetchSubsM is called only from the MOVIE rename path (executeOne); the TV rename path (executeEpisode) has no equivalent call.
Muxing into the container would require an ffmpeg remux step that does not exist (same missing capability as the Relang apply).
Consequence: Kodi/Jellyfin will pick up the sidecars for movies, but episodic TV gets no subtitles at all, and no media gets embedded subs. README documents both gaps honestly under 'What's next'.

openIssues.name: DuplicatesGroupedIntoEditionsButNotRankedForUserDecision
openIssues.what: Exact byte-duplicates (same CRC tag + matching size at the target) are removed at rename, and distinct rips of one tmdb_id are clustered into editions by runtime, but multiple DISTINCT rips of the same cut are never ranked by quality and surfaced for a keep/discard decision.
why: executeOne removes a source that is byte-identical to something already at the target (DuplicateRemoved). Versions.analyze clusters by cut and even computes qualityScore and picks a per-edition default. But that is as far as it goes.

qualityScore exists (resolution/depth/bitrate/codec/channels weighting) and analyze marks an is_default member, yet nothing presents 'you have a 1080p x264 and a 2160p x265 of the same cut, keep which?' to the user or auto-prunes the loser.
The editions/versions tables capture the grouping; the missing piece is a surfacing/pruning verb. README lists this under 'What's next' as duplicate management.
blocking: automated or assisted pruning of redundant quality variants

openIssues.name: NoRematchGateBeforePromotion
openIssues.what: move trusts the tmdb id written into the buffer NFO by rename and does not re-verify the match against TMDB before promoting into the library.
why: moveFolder parses the buffer NFO, reads its tmdb id, and promotes. If rename associated the wrong title, move faithfully promotes the wrong title; the only verification at this stage is byte-identity (size), not correctness of the MATCH.
This is by design for now: the buffer is the human review step, and re-matching at promotion would re-incur TMDB calls and could disagree with a deliberate manual correction in the buffer.
README flags an optional re-match gate under 'What's next'. If added, it would re-run the resolver against the buffer NFO id and refuse/flag on disagreement.
blocking: catching a mis-association before it reaches the library

openIssues.name: BatchTvResolveNeverPromptsAndAutoRefusesAmbiguousShows
openIssues.what: The TvInteract ability and batchInteract handler exist, but Tv.Resolve.resolveOne never calls chooseShow; ambiguous shows are resolved purely by pickBestShow's popularity tiebreak, and a no-confident-match becomes a silent NoShowMatch refusal.
why: batchInteract is a handler that auto-answers chooseShow with None, i.e. 'never pick interactively'. The interactive picker is plumbed as an ability but resolveShowPick decides via scoreShow + pickBestShow and surfaces NoShowMatch when nothing scores high enough.

So in batch mode an ambiguous show is refused rather than queued for a human, and there is no --interactive path wired into the TV resolver run (unlike the movie/interactive show selection mentioned for the broader project).
Wiring an interactive handler would mean swapping batchInteract for one that prompts, and threading a flag through Tv.Resolve.run / runWith.
blocking: human disambiguation of ambiguous TV show matches in batch runs

Config.fromEnv: reads UNIDORK_* env vars with HARDCODED fallbacks baked into the source (db host localhost, port 5434, user postgres, name dork; specific NAS paths under /home/bismuth). nix/config.nix is expected to set these env vars; the literals here are last-resort defaults, not the production config.
performs IO (getEnv) and never fails: every missing var resolves to its fallback.
the movie/tv format strings are also fallback literals here; production format strings come from UNIDORK_FORMAT_MOVIE / UNIDORK_FORMAT_TV.
Config.getEnvOr: empty OR whitespace-only env values are treated as UNSET and resolve to the fallback (Text.trim then size==0 check), not returned as empty strings.
a getEnv that throws (Left) also resolves to the fallback; no exception escapes.
Move.removeFolderTree: shells out to `rm -rf --`; this is the one place the system recursively deletes a tree.
refuses to run on '', '/', or any non-absolute path (must startWith '/'), returning Left rather than executing. This guard is the backstop against a catastrophic rm.
a nonzero rm exit is returned as Left with the captured stderr, not raised.
Move.commitFolder: shells `mv -T -- src dst`; -T forces dst to be treated as a name, not a directory to move INTO. This is the point of no return for a same-filesystem promotion.
nonzero exit -> Left with stderr; success -> Right (). Does not itself check enforceUnderRoot; the caller must have done that.
Move.transferFolder: branches on sameDev: same device -> atomic commitFolder; cross device -> rsync to partialRoot, then commitFolder, then removeFolderTree on the source.
on a cross-device ABORT (rsync or commit fails) the source is LEFT INTACT and false is returned; only a fully successful commit triggers source deletion.
source-cleanup failure after a successful commit is a WARN, not a failure: the file is already safely in the library, so a leftover source is logged and tolerated (returns true).
Move.verifyFile: verified == (file exists in files table by path) AND (on-disk size == stored size_bytes). It does NOT re-hash; a size match means the stored CRC is trusted as-is (see decision IdentityVerifiedBySizeNotByRehash).
a missing files row or a stat failure yields (path, false, ...) and routes the caller to a name-based update with a WARN.
Move.moveFolder: aborts (prints, does nothing) if the destination is not under the library root OR already exists; it can never overwrite an existing library folder.
on a real (non-dry) run it transfers then DELETES the source folder from the buffer; on dry-run it prints the plan and touches nothing.
runs under the MovieMoveCatalog ability: the files-row path update is an ability call interpreted at the run boundary, not a direct DB write here.
Move.run: processes buffer folders in chunks of moveChunkSize (25), opening a fresh prepared-statement set per chunk inside its own singleIO connection; a crash in one chunk does not corrupt the connection used by others.
calls sweepPartial(libraryRoot) once before any real transfer to clear crashed-partial debris (skipped on dry-run).
a single-folder name argument is validated against '', '.', '..' and refused if invalid; the no-argument form promotes every buffer subdirectory.
Move.sameDevice: compares `stat %d` device numbers of the two paths; equal device -> true.
if EITHER stat fails it returns false, deliberately choosing the safer cross-device (rsync-partial) path over risking a non-atomic rename.
Stage.runRhashCrc32: shells `rhash --crc32 -p %C`; the output is uppercased AND trimmed before returning. The ENTIRE pipeline compares CRCs in uppercase, so any CRC that bypasses this normalization will silently fail to match.
nonzero exit -> Left; no exception escapes.
Stage.probeWithCrc: hashes FIRST (runRhashCrc32) and short-circuits on hash failure before ever invoking ffprobe; a file that cannot be hashed is never probed.
performs two subprocess executions (rhash then ffprobe) per call.
Stage.partitionWork: drops items whose probe_cache row is fresh (mtime >= cached mtime AND size matches), so already-probed unchanged files are skipped without re-probing.
an item that cannot be stat'd is KEPT (size 0) rather than dropped, so a transiently unreadable file is retried rather than silently skipped.
the surviving work is returned sorted by size.
Stage.upsertFileSql: ON CONFLICT (crc32, size_bytes) the hint_* columns use COALESCE(EXCLUDED, existing): a re-probe that finds no NFO hint will NOT erase a hint recorded by an earlier pass. stage and probe payload, by contrast, are overwritten wholesale.
this is why re-running probe after a hint was set is safe; the hint is sticky.
Stage.upsertFileWith: wraps the bind/execute in catch and DISCARDS failures: a per-file DB error silently drops that row and the batch continues. There is no per-row error surfaced to the caller.
runs under Postgres only; the connection is supplied by the chunk runner.
Stage.ProbeResult.fromJson: accepts BOTH the current 'audios' array and a LEGACY single 'audio' object (falls back to wrapping it in a one-element list); missing 'subtitles' decodes to [].
this dual shape is what lets old cached probe_json rows still decode after the multi-audio schema change.
Stage.bitDepthFrom: prefers bits_per_raw_sample when present; otherwise INFERS depth from the pixel format string (p10/10le/10be -> 10, p12/... -> 12, else 8).
the inference is a substring scan on pix_fmt, so an unusual pix_fmt naming could mis-infer; absent any signal it defaults to 8.
Stage.forkChunk: forks one concurrent probe per item in the chunk and then reads all promises; probing is parallel within a chunk.
per-file probe failures are LOGGED (FAIL line) and collected as Left, never fatal; the chunk completes regardless of individual failures.
Resolve.resolveOne: match priority: an NFO tmdb id hint wins outright at confidence 100 with source 'nfo_id'; otherwise title/year (from hint or parsed from the name) is searched, candidates scored, and ties broken by runtime proximity (pickBestWithRuntime).
the dry-run gate lives HERE: on dryRun it computes the same outcome but does not call recordMatch (verified by the dryRunNoWrite test).
no DB or HTTP directly; everything goes through the MetaApi/ResolveCatalog abilities (see decision DatabaseAndMetadataAreAbilitiesInterpretedAtRunBoundary).
Tmdb.runtimeWinner: used to break a scoring tie by fetching each tied candidate's TMDB runtime and keeping only those within 15 minutes (tolerance) of the probed runtime; returns Some only if EXACTLY ONE candidate falls in range.
issues a movieDetails MetaApi call per tied candidate, so a tie among many candidates costs many detail fetches.
a candidate whose TMDB runtime is 0 (unknown) is excluded from the in-range set rather than treated as matching.
Tmdb.scoreCandidate: additive score: id match +50, exact normalized-title match +30 (else token-overlap >=75% +20, >=50% +10), exact year +20 (off-by-one +10). A perfect match tops out at 100; the resolver's tiedAtBest threshold is 40.
title comparison runs through Tmdb.normalize (lowercase, unicode-punctuation folding, leading-article stripping), so 'The Matrix' and 'matrix' compare equal.
kernel.score.resolveTie: a single candidate wins automatically; with several, the popularity winner is taken ONLY if its popularity exceeds the runner-up's by the popularityRatio (3x) factor, otherwise the tie is declared unresolvable (None).
this is a deliberate refusal: an ambiguous tie returns None rather than guessing, so the file goes unresolved instead of mis-associated.
Tv.Parse.refFromToken: parses an episode token in several shapes: SxxEyy, multi-ep SxxEyyEzz / SxxEyy-Ezz / SxxEyy-zz, and the alternate NxM form (1x02). Up to 3 episode numbers per ref; each <= 999.

season 0 is the 'specials' bucket: S00Exx keeps season 0, and notably S04E00 (and any all-zero episode list) collapses to season 0 as well, treating a zero episode as a special rather than a real S04 episode.

rejects look-alikes that are NOT episode refs: se7en, sample, soundtrack, S01 (no episode), S01E (empty), S01E02v2 (trailing junk), and resolution tokens 1920x1080 / 1280x720 (the NxM guard requires season <= 99).
Tv.Resolve.resolveOne: show-match priority: direct NFO tmdb id (nfo_id, conf 100) or {tmdb-...} folder tag (folder_tag, 100); else imdb id from hint or {imdb-...} folder tag resolved via DB then TMDB find (imdb_find, 95); else title/year search scored by scoreShow (title_year).
REFUSES the whole file (TvEpisodeMissing, no write) if ANY requested episode number is absent from the fetched TMDB season; it will not partially associate.
dry-run gate is here: recordEpisodeMatch is skipped on dryRun.
the episode ref comes from the filename first (parseEpisodeName) and falls back to season-from-folders + bare episode number (refFromFolders).
Tv.Resolve.batchInteract: a TvInteract handler that ALWAYS answers chooseShow with None; installing it means ambiguous shows are never prompted and instead fall through to scoring/refusal (see open issue BatchTvResolveNeverPromptsAndAutoRefusesAmbiguousShows).
Tv.Move.mergeTree: recursively merges src into an EXISTING destination tree: directories recurse, files are moved, but an existing video file at the destination is SKIPPED (printed 'skip (exists)'), never overwritten.
this is the wider-blast-radius path that distinguishes tv-move from movie move; it can touch an already-populated show folder but cannot clobber an episode already there.
removes the now-emptied source folder (rmdirFolder) at the end.
Rename.executeOne: if a CRC-tagged entry already exists at the target AND its size matches, the source is treated as a verified byte-duplicate and REMOVED (DuplicateRemoved); a CRC-tagged entry whose size does NOT match is a Conflict (left in place).

writes the NFO and renames the video INTO the buffer (not the library); on success it also fetches sidecar subtitles, records promoteToBuffer, refreshes probe_cache for the new path, and deletes the old path's probe_cache row.
dry-run yields WouldRename / WouldRemoveDuplicate and performs no filesystem mutation.
kernel.cache.Cached.fromJson: decodes the cache 'key' field but FALLS BACK to a legacy 'folder' field when 'key' is absent, so old cache rows written under the previous schema still decode (covered by the legacyKey test).
Db.upsertMovieSql: ON CONFLICT (folder_checksum) the actual_runtime_sec column uses COALESCE(EXCLUDED, existing): an upsert that lacks a freshly-probed runtime will NOT null out a runtime recorded earlier. Most other columns are overwritten from EXCLUDED.
keyed on folder_checksum, not on the (crc, size) file identity; this is the LIBRARY catalogue row, distinct from the files row.
Versions.clusterByCut: clusters by normalized seconds (frame-rate canceled) with a 1.5% relative tolerance, so a PAL 25fps copy and a 23.976fps copy of the same cut land in ONE cluster while a genuine extended cut splits off (verified by palSameCut and clusterSeparatesRealCut tests).
input is sorted by normalized seconds first, then a single forward pass groups adjacent copies against the cluster anchor.
Versions.normalizedSeconds: = durationSec * fps / referenceFps, canceling frame-rate speedup against the 24000/1001 reference; a copy with fps 0 (unknown) falls back to raw durationSec rather than dividing.
this is the value clustering compares, NOT the raw probed duration.
Versions.qualityScore: a single packed Nat ranking copies by, in descending weight: resolution rank, bit depth, bitrate (Mbps), video codec rank, audio channels, audio codec rank. Higher is better; used to pick the default member of an edition.
the score is computed but, beyond choosing a per-edition default, is not yet used to prune or surface redundant rips (see open issue DuplicatesGroupedIntoEditionsButNotRankedForUserDecision).
Tv.Tmdb.scoreShow: additive like the movie scorer but with a higher exact-title weight (+40 vs +30): id match +50, exact normalized name +40 (else overlap >=75% +20, >=50% +10), exact year +20 (off-by-one +10).
compares both name and original_name through Tmdb.normalize and takes the better overlap.
Tv.Stage.collectVideos: recurses subdirectories only up to maxDepth (4) and SKIPS extras/sample directories (isExtrasDir) and sample-named files (isSampleName), so featurettes/trailers/proof dirs never enter the episode pipeline.
the depth bound is a guard against pathological nesting, not a correctness requirement.
Tv.Stage.episodeHints: derives (title, year, showId, imdbId, season, episode) hints from the filename first, then the show folder, then the immediate folder's tvshow.nfo, then the top folder's tvshow.nfo; the tmdb id and imdb id are read from NFO/scan, season+episode from the parsed ref.
imdb scanning is skipped entirely once a tmdb show id is found (the showId branch short-circuits the imdbId branch), so the cheaper NFO id wins over a folder imdb scan.
